quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should passengers do while riding?

options.text: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold onto the rider's hips, waist, or belt.
questions.explanation: Before riding, tell your passenger to hold firmly to your hips, waist, or belt. If your motorcycle has secure handholds, the passenger can use those instead.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of a lane behind a car, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can block the use of a side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, who goes first?

options.text: The vehicle on the right goes first. The vehicle on the left must yield.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the right goes first. The vehicle on the left must yield.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a green signal before turning in that direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When you take alcohol and drugs together, what happens?

options.text: The effects are less dangerous than using either alone.
The effects cancel each other out.
The effects are stronger than using either alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects are stronger than using either alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can affect your riding. Combining drugs with alcohol makes the danger much worse.

questions.question: How fast does your body remove alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at about one drink per hour on average. This varies by person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What can a plastic face shield protect you from?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your face during a crash. It also protects you from everyday hazards like rocks from other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you apply the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle on the road?

options.text: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
Without any wheel or fender touching the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. One wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake on a motorcycle is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: _________ of motorcycle and car collisions happen because the driver did not yield the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.
questions.correctAnswerText: More than half
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle and car collisions happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Never assume that other drivers will yield, even if they are supposed to.

questions.question: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. U.S. motorcycles made after 1978 turn the headlight on automatically when the engine runs. Check that it works before every ride.

questions.question: You should use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch when:

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch right away. This removes power from the rear wheel so you can safely leave the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign appears on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel slower than 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:

options.text: Is always the left portion of the lane.
Is always the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes depending on the situation.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always safest. Change your position in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How far in advance should you signal a turn on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal a left or right turn 100 feet before you turn. This gives other drivers time to safely react to your move.

questions.question: A benefit of keeping space between you and other vehicles is that:

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles better.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. If a danger appears, you will have more time to respond and more room to move safely.

questions.question: If another driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: You know that they have seen you.
It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
They will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not always mean they have actually seen you.
questions.explanation: Do not trust eye contact as proof that a driver sees you. A driver can look directly at a motorcycle and still not notice it.

questions.question: The best way to stay safe while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
Ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Scan the road far ahead of you while riding. Watch for dangers before you reach them so you can react in time.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, your main concern should be the helmet's:
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection.
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: Small vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast a small vehicle is going or how far away it is. Do not assume other drivers can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: When wearing a helmet during a crash, a rider is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than someone not wearing a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as someone not wearing a helmet.
More likely to survive than someone not wearing a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than someone not wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders with helmets, no matter the speed.

questions.question: Motorcyclists can use HOV lanes:

options.text: But only if they are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Unless otherwise posted.
questions.explanation: In California, motorcyclists can generally use High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes. Always obey any signs that say motorcyclists cannot use HOV lanes.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: When braking a motorcycle:

options.text: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. Using only the rear brake may prevent you from developing the skill to use the front brake correctly in an emergency stop.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT have a major effect on blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.correctAnswerText: Age
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content is affected by how much you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.correctAnswerText: Quieter than
questions.explanation: Motorcycle horns are not as loud as car horns. Use your horn when needed, but do not depend on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, a motorcyclist has an advantage over a car driver because:

options.text: The motorcycle can speed up faster than a car.
The motorcyclist can ride in the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcyclist can ride in the left part of the lane to avoid people and cars on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles on your right, you can ride in the left part of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between vehicles. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.
